Addressed by #38983. `State.commit` now installs the rebuilt state before running domain finalizers, so public update events are read barriers: subscribers that refetch after `agent.updated`, `command.updated`, `catalog.updated`, `skill.updated`, `websearch.updated`, `integration.updated`, or reference updates observe committed state. The PR audited every finalizer and adds a regression test that failed under the old ordering. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #39126, building on the native provider PDF lowering from #38253. The V2 Read tool now recognizes PDFs, returns bounded native model file content under the media ingest policy, preserves typed errors for malformed or invalid inputs, and exposes Read paths through ACP. Focused Core and ACP tests and typechecks passed. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

This looks really awesome. I'm eager to get otel really wired up with opencode for a project I am working on. I can sort of hack opencode with the popular otel plugin to do what I want with modifications, but it would be great if opencode itself would accept traceparent header and stamp that on all the otel related traces like tools, sessions, etc.

I had AI write up some of my thoughts that I had it scan everywhere trying to see what was in the works for otel in v2, seems like otel issues/prs arent going anywhere in 1.X, likely in favor of v2 which makes a ton of sense.


One thing I'd love to see: could opencode accept a `traceparent` on the API (and ideally on the websocket path too) and use it as the parent for that turn?

### What we're after

We run `opencode serve` long-lived in a sandbox and dispatch each turn over HTTP from our own service. Right now our spans and opencode's spans both make it to the backend fine, they just sit in separate traces, so you can't see the whole thing as one flamegraph. In Datadog or SigNoz it'd be really nice to click into a request and see the turn, the model calls and the tool calls hanging underneath whatever actually kicked it off.

`OPENCODE_TRACEPARENT` doesn't work for our setup because the server outlives any single request, so it's either one giant unbounded trace or nothing.

### On the per-turn root thing

I saw each turn is deliberately its own root trace and I think that's the right default, a conversation span held open for hours would be worse. This wouldn't really change that. It'd still be one trace per turn, just rooted at the caller when a caller passes context.

### Looks mostly wired already?

`SessionTelemetry.TraceParent` takes an `AnySpan` and `Tracer.externalSpan()` is exactly what you get from decoding a traceparent, so it seems like mostly a question of getting the header into that reference.

Also worth mentioning #37395 landed on v2 after you opened this and makes the server pick up inbound traceparent on request fibers, so you might end up in this code on rebase anyway.

### Couple of things to consider

On websockets it'd have to ride on the message rather than the upgrade, since the connection isn't the turn.

And since message content can come from untrusted places it probably wants to be opt-in, so nobody can graft their spans onto someone else's trace.

### Otherwise

If parenting isn't something you want to do here, even just a span link to the inbound context would help.

Happy to test against a real OTLP stack if that's useful.

I reproduced this on OpenCode 1.18.7 and found one concrete cause for the discrepancy between `opencode debug skill` and the full TUI.

The affected `SKILL.md` contained an unquoted colon followed by a space in its YAML description:

```yaml
---
name: work-jira-issue
description: Use when working a Jira issue end-to-end: retrieve issue context, implement code changes, and create a PR.
```

Observed behavior:
- opencode debug skill listed the skill successfully.
- The HTTP /skill endpoint and opencode --mini also listed it.
- Full TUI startup silently excluded it and logged init count=4.
- The skill was absent from <available_skills>.
- A direct skill("work-jira-issue") call returned “not found.”
- No frontmatter parsing error appeared in the startup log.

Rewriting the description without `:` fixed full-TUI discovery:

```yaml
description: Use when working a Jira issue end-to-end by retrieving context, implementing changes, and creating a PR.
```

Afterward, full TUI startup logged the skill and init count=5.
Quoting the original description also worked. This is related to #6858, but the current failure mode is different: instead of crashing, OpenCode 1.18.7 exposes the malformed skill through debug skill while silently dropping it from the full TUI/model-facing registry.
It would help if all discovery paths used the same frontmatter validation and reported the offending file and YAML error.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #36443: Scoping event subscriptions by client interest (server-side fix for the same event fan-out root cause)
- #37792: TUI ignoring foreign-session events (client-side filtering for a closely related problem)
- #36441: Umbrella tracking issue for event stream scoping

Your issue adds a concrete multi-TUI reproduction path and specifically identifies the `?directory=` parameter being ignored on `/global/event`, which complements the analysis in those issues.

Same root cause family, but I do not think this is a duplicate. Two differences: the transport and the event types.

Those three are all about the v2 `/api/event` stream in `packages/server`, and all three are labelled 2.0. #37792 points at `packages/tui/src/context/client.tsx`, which does not exist on `dev` yet, it arrives with #37486/#37487.

What I hit is the v1 `/global/event` route in `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/global.ts`, which is what the shipping 1.18.x TUI actually subscribes to at `packages/tui/src/context/sdk.tsx:91`. On `dev` the v2 `DataProvider` is fed off that same stream through `useEvent` at `packages/tui/src/context/data.tsx:75`, so `packages/tui/src/context/event.ts` is the single seam today.

The other difference is the axis. #36443 and #37792 scope by session interest. Neither of my symptoms carries a session:

- `vcs.branch.updated` has no session at all
- `tui.session.select` is deliberately addressed at a TUI, not at a session

So a session interest gate does not filter either one. The branch would still be wrong and the wrong TUI would still get navigated. #36443 does list location scoping in its acceptance criteria, which would cover this, but on the v2 transport whenever that lands.

Last one is that these are correctness bugs on a released build rather than fan-out cost. Wrong branch rendered in the sidebar, wrong TUI navigated on a session switch.

Happy to close this and fold it under #36441 if you would rather keep it all in one place. Otherwise I have a fix for the v1 path that scopes `vcs.branch.updated`, `tui.session.select`, `tui.toast.show`, `tui.command.execute` and `tui.prompt.append` by directory and leaves session and message events unfiltered, since a TUI can legitimately hold sessions from sibling directories of the same project.
